text.en: Meena touches the tea and says it is hot, then the juice and says it is cold. But touch can fool us. A cold hand can make warm water feel hot. We need a better way: the thermometer.

Our sense of touch is not reliable for judging hot and cold. Put one hand in cold water and the other in warm water, then both in lukewarm water, and the two hands feel different. To measure how hot or cold something is, we use temperature.
Temperature tells us how hot or cold an object is. It is not the same as heat, which is a form of energy. Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius.
A clinical thermometer measures body temperature. It reads from 35 to 42 degrees Celsius and has a kink that stops the mercury from falling back. A laboratory thermometer measures from -10 to 110 degrees Celsius and is used for water and other things. Normal human body temperature is about 37 degrees Celsius.
Wash it before and after, shake the mercury down below the normal reading for a clinical thermometer, then place it under the tongue or arm. For a laboratory thermometer, keep the bulb in the liquid and not touching the sides. Read at eye level. Never hold a clinical thermometer in hot water.

problem.en: Normal body temperature is 37 degrees. A child has 39. By how much is it high?

prompt.en: Why can you not trust your hand to measure temperature?

requiredIdeas.en: The hand feels relative to its own state.
A thermometer gives a number everyone can agree on.

points.en: Touch is unreliable; use a thermometer.
Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius.
Keep the bulb in the liquid and read at eye level.
